title: Christy's "Signing of the Constitution"
content: Howard Chandler Christy's painting called "Scene at the Signing of the Constitution of the United States" shows George Washington standing at the dais and Benjamin Franklin seated at center.Christy researched the subject for five years and spent seven months painting it. He studied portraits of almost all of the people represented, and he looked for whatever authentic props he could find.TheSmithsonian Institutionlent him George Washington's breeches, and The Library of Congress let him borrow some of Thomas Jefferson's books, which appear next to Franklin’s chair. The painting hangs in theCapitol buildingin the east stairway of theHouse of Representatives.
